highlights: Imperial Beijing sanctuary with seductive Forbidden City views and rooftop garden terraces
description:
Mandarin Oriental Wangfujing occupies a rare perch above WF CENTRAL on No. 269 Wangfujing Street, in Dongcheng District, where Beijing's premier shopping avenue approaches the ceremonial heart of the capital. From here, the Forbidden City and Tiananmen Square are a short stroll away, the hutongs sit minutes from the door, and the Temple of Heaven and Great Wall remain natural extensions of an imperial itinerary.

The hotel is intimate by Beijing standards, with 73 rooms and suites that begin at a generous 55 square metres. Floor-to-ceiling windows, marble bathrooms and a pale contemporary palette create a polished urban calm, while many rooms frame the palace roofs and the city's historic axis. A landscaped rooftop garden and terraces give the property a sense of space unusual for Wangfujing, especially at sunset.

Dining is arranged around the view as much as the plate. Café Zi serves contemporary Cantonese and regional Chinese cooking, Mandarin Grill brings classic steakhouse seafood and beef, and MO Bar works into the evening with cocktails and an outdoor terrace facing the Forbidden City. The Library and Mandarin Cake Shop add quieter ritual to the day, while WF CENTRAL's boutiques and restaurants sit directly below.

The Spa has four suites, including one configured for Moroccan hammam-style water treatments, alongside a skylit 25-metre swimming pool and a modern fitness centre. For a city hotel, the mood feels unusually composed: a refined base for shopping, serious sightseeing and quiet evenings above one of Beijing's most storied streets. The small scale keeps the experience discreet, without losing the confidence of a major Mandarin Oriental address.

highlights: Taikoo Hui glamour with expansive rooms, serious Cantonese dining and Tianhe skyline polish
description:
Mandarin Oriental, Guangzhou rises at 389 Tianhe Road in the city's modern commercial core, directly beside Taikoo Hui and connected to Shipaiqiao metro station. The setting places the hotel close to the business addresses of Tianhe, with swift access to Guangzhou East railway station for Hong Kong-bound trains and easy connections to the wider city's temples, museums and Pearl River landmarks. Its mall-level access makes retail and dining part of the daily rhythm.

The hotel has 233 rooms and 30 suites, among the most spacious in Guangzhou, plus a collection of serviced apartments. Interiors balance a clean-lined contemporary mood with Chinese detail: deep timber tones, generous bathrooms, dressing areas and broad city views give even the entry categories a residential feel. The Oriental Club adds a more private rhythm on the higher floors.

Cantonese dining is a defining strength. Jiang by Chef Fei holds two MICHELIN stars in the 2025 Guangzhou Guide and gives the hotel an assured culinary anchor, while TANG brings a modern Chinese bistro sensibility. The Loft, LIÁNG and the Mandarin Oriental Cake Shop cover cocktails, whisky, afternoon tea and patisserie, giving the property a notably complete urban dining circuit.

Wellness is equally substantial for an urban property. The spa includes six individual treatment suites, three couples' suites including a VIP suite, steam rooms, saunas, vitality pools and experience showers. A 25-metre temperature-controlled outdoor pool, private sundeck with massage pavilions, fitness centre and family amenities make the hotel feel less like a business-district address and more like a polished Tianhe retreat.

highlights: Sky-high Futian retreat with park-framed views, sculptural design and dazzling rooftop energy
description:
Mandarin Oriental Shenzhen occupies the upper levels of Block A at UpperHills, No. 5001 Huanggang Road, in Futian District. The address puts the hotel within one of Shenzhen's most ambitious mixed-use developments, next to luxury retail and lifestyle outlets and between two of the city's green landmarks, Bijia Hill Park and Lotus Hill Park. High-speed rail, ferry terminals and airport road links are all within practical reach.

The 178 rooms and suites sit high above the city, with floor-to-ceiling glass framing Futian's towers, Shenzhen Bay, nearby parks and, on clear days, the distant mountains of Hong Kong. Rooms start at 56 square metres and are among the largest in Shenzhen, combining marble bathrooms, walk-in wardrobes and contemporary East-meets-West detailing with high-spec technology. The Mandarin Club on the 78th floor adds a further layer of privacy.

Dining gives the hotel a strong social pulse. The Bay by Chef Fei leads the restaurant collection with refined Cantonese cooking, while OPUS 388 focuses on prime meat and seafood, RIN offers private Japanese dining, TAPAS 77 brings a Spanish note, Bazaar spans Asian café dishes, and LIAN Lounge, MO Bar and The Mandarin Cake Shop cover tea, cocktails and sweets.

The wellness spaces are deliberately theatrical. The Spa includes seven treatment suites, five with 68th-floor views, plus a suite with a heated quartz sand bed. A pool beneath a 30-metre-high ceiling and a fitness centre with city views turn the upper floors into a vertical sanctuary, well suited to a hotel that treats Shenzhen's restless skyline as part of the experience.

highlights: Palatial Taipei landmark with lavish European grandeur, MICHELIN-starred Cantonese dining and grand salons
description:
Mandarin Oriental, Taipei stands on tree-lined Dunhua North Road in Songshan District, at the edge of one of the capital's established business and cultural corridors. Taipei Arena and Nanjing Fuxing MRT stations are close by, while Xinyi, Taipei 101 and the city's major shopping and entertainment addresses are typically a short drive away. Songshan Airport is also close, reinforcing the hotel's business-friendly position.

The hotel is grand rather than minimal, with European-influenced architecture, arched forms, chandeliers, marble and a sense of ceremony that distinguishes it from Taipei's glassier luxury towers. Its 256 rooms and 47 suites are among the city's most spacious, pairing walk-in wardrobes and marble bathrooms with rich classical detailing. Club guests have access to The Oriental Lounge, adding a quieter residential dimension.

Dining is one of the property's strongest calling cards. Ya Ge, the elegant Chinese restaurant, holds one MICHELIN star in the 2025 Taiwan Guide and has been recognised for eight consecutive years. Bencotto serves contemporary Italian cuisine, Café Un Deux Trois operates as the relaxed international venue, The Jade Lounge is a polished setting for afternoon tea, and M.O. Bar brings an Art Deco mood to cocktails.

The spa extends over two floors with 12 treatment suites, including couples' and VIP double suites, heat and water experiences, a 20-metre outdoor pool, a fitness and wellness centre, Kinesis equipment and a functional studio. With major ballrooms and salons also on site, the hotel feels both urban and ceremonial: a Taipei landmark designed for stays, dining and grand occasions alike.

local_area: Via Rinaldo Menardi, near Cortina centre
highlights: Historic Dolomite grande dame reborn with Alpine glamour, terraces and year-round mountain adventure
description:
Mandarin Oriental Cortina is planned to open in early 2027 as Mandarin Oriental Cristallo, Cortina, returning the historic Cristallo address on Via Rinaldo Menardi to the Dolomite hotel scene after a major transformation. The setting is minutes from the centre of Cortina d'Ampezzo, with terraces and views oriented toward one of Italy's most dramatic Alpine landscapes and the resort's year-round sporting culture.

The official plans describe 84 guest rooms and elegant suites, many looking toward the surrounding peaks. The tone is expected to preserve the property's historic mountain presence while introducing Mandarin Oriental's contemporary approach to comfort, wellness and service. In a resort town long associated with winter glamour, climbing culture and summer mountain air, that balance of heritage and modernity is essential.

Dining is planned around a collection of restaurants and bars with a modern Italian sensibility. A signature restaurant with a new terrace is positioned as the social centre of the property, designed for drinks and meals against the mountain backdrop rather than enclosed resort formality. Exact venue names have not yet been publicly finalised.

Wellness and outdoor access are the other anchors. The Spa is described as a restorative retreat for days spent on the slopes or on hiking trails, and the wider setting gives natural access to Cortina's ski terrain in winter and Dolomite walking routes in summer. Because the hotel has not yet opened, some operational details remain limited; what is clear is the ambition to revive a historic Alpine grande dame as a year-round mountain resort.
